text: Compare Fine-Gray model Aalen-Johansen baseline using 3-fold CV four built-tasks. Fine-Gray pipeline uses mlr3pipelines encode factor predictors standardize features numerical stability.
code: library(mlr3cmprsk) library(mlr3pipelines) set.seed(42L)  tasks = tsks(c("pbc", "transplant", "mgus2", "hoel")) tasks$pbc$select(c("age", "chol", "albumin", "bili")) # Stratify by event status so all splits keep all available causes for (task in tasks) {   task$set_col_roles(task$target_names[2L], add_to = "stratum") }  learner1 = as_learner(   po("encode", method = "treatment") %>>% po("scale") %>>% lrn("cmprsk.fg") ) learner1$id = "cmprsk.fg" learner2 = lrn("cmprsk.aalen") learners = list(learner1, learner2)  bm_grid = benchmark_grid(tasks, learners, rsmp("cv", folds = 3L)) bm = benchmark(bm_grid)  measures = list(   # AUC and Brier score at each test fold's median follow-up time, which is in   # months for `mgus2`, and days for the other tasks   msr("cmprsk.auc", id = "auc"),   msr("cmprsk.brier", id = "brier"),   # IBS: 50 equally spaced times from 0 to each test fold's 90th follow-up percentile   msr("cmprsk.ibs", ntimes = 50, id = "ibs") )  # By default, each measure averages the cause-specific scores, with weights # equal to the observed event frequencies in each test fold bm$aggregate(measures)[, .(task_id, learner_id, auc, brier, ibs)] ##       task_id   learner_id       auc     brier        ibs ## 1:        pbc    cmprsk.fg 0.8509168 0.1180410 0.10811066 ## 2:        pbc cmprsk.aalen 0.5000000 0.1800472 0.15472607 ## 3: transplant    cmprsk.fg 0.7817820 0.1553654 0.14468693 ## 4: transplant cmprsk.aalen 0.5000000 0.2160769 0.18127722 ## 5:      mgus2    cmprsk.fg 0.7219273 0.1842674 0.15657283 ## 6:      mgus2 cmprsk.aalen 0.5000000 0.2182213 0.18878181 ## 7:       hoel    cmprsk.fg 0.5261999 0.1362216 0.09429959 ## 8:       hoel cmprsk.aalen 0.5000000 0.1361634 0.09460271

Every entry must finite strictly positive, sum must exceed 1. remaining probability specifies censoring; sum 1 disables censoring. probabilities hold theoretically beta_sd = 0, approximate covariate effects. Define \(r_{ik} = \lambda_k \exp(x_i^\top \beta_k)\) \(R_i = \sum_{k=1}^K r_{ik}\). cumulative hazards overall event-free survival function, conditional covariates, $$H_{ik}(t) = r_{ik} t^\gamma, \qquad H_i(t) = R_i t^\gamma,$$ $$S_i(t) = \exp(-R_i t^\gamma).$$ quantities \(r_{ik}\) \(R_i\) cumulative-hazard coefficients, corresponding constant hazard rates \(\gamma = 1\). simulate uncensored event time, draw \(E_i \sim \mathrm{Exp}(1)\) set $$Y_i = (E_i / R_i)^{1/\gamma}.$$ event cause \(J_i\) sampled probabilities \(P(J_i = k \mid x_i) = r_{ik}/R_i\). cause-specific hazards share Weibull shape, event cause uncensored event time conditionally independent given covariates. follows cause-specific hazard-based simulation framework Beyersmann et al. (2009). Censoring generated independently covariates event process. Let \(p_0 = 1 - \sum_{k=1}^K p_k\) \(\lambda_C = \mathrm{rate} \cdot p_0\). Draw \(E_{Ci} \sim \mathrm{Exp}(1)\) independently set $$C_i = (E_{Ci} / \lambda_C)^{1/\gamma}.$$ \(p_0 = 0\), set \(C_i = \infty\), corresponding censoring. observed time \(T_i = \min(Y_i, C_i)\), observed event indicator \(\delta_i = J_i\) \(Y_i \le C_i\), \(\delta_i = 0\) otherwise. model, cause-specific cumulative incidence functions analytical form $$F_{ik}(t) = \frac{r_{ik}}{R_i}   \left(1 - \exp(-R_i t^\gamma)\right),$$ satisfying \(\sum_{k=1}^K F_{ik}(t) = 1 - S_i(t)\). conditional probability observing cause \(k\) \(r_{ik}/(R_i + \lambda_C)\), probability censoring \(\lambda_C/(R_i + \lambda_C)\).
